display.purpose: The counts in the Overview status strip.

headline.purpose: Page titles and empty-state headings; the instance hero runs clamp(20px, 2.2vw, 26px), dialog titles 17px/650.

label.purpose: Buttons, tabs, nav items, segmented controls, field labels.

caption.purpose: Table headers, status pills, legends and side notes.

data.purpose: Machine values: ids, timestamps, durations, numeric cells, chart axes and payloads.

shadows.name: contact
shadows.purpose: Resting buttons, inputs, panels, cards, the status strip, failure groups (dark: 0 1px 2px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)).

shadows.name: lifted
shadows.purpose: Only what floats: popovers, menus, dialogs, toasts, the bulk bar, the peek panel, the phone sheet.

shadows.name: lifted-dark
shadows.purpose: The lifted shadow in dark mode.

shadows.name: sheen-dark
shadows.purpose: Top-edge highlight on panels, cards and the hero in dark mode.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Every focus-visible element; the ring is the theme's accent (lighter in dark).

shadows.name: veil
shadows.purpose: Overlay behind dialogs and sheets (dark: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6)).

motion.name: hover-fade
motion.purpose: Background and border colour on the way into a hover only; theme and mode changes apply at once.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Applied to everything under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

narrative.overview:
DfMon is a contemporary developer console held to the craft level of Linear, Vercel, Trigger.dev and Inngest. The surfaces are calm and neutral: a near-white or near-black ground, panels one step off it, structure drawn with 1px low-contrast hairlines, one confident accent per theme. Everything else is turned down so that status colour and the onset of failures are the loudest things on any screen. An operator on a bad day reads the hub's health from one strip, sees where failures began, and reaches the failing thing in a click.

The system is one family, studio, with four themes that share every shape, type and status rule and differ only in their neutrals and their accent: Iris (indigo on cool grey, the default), Jade (teal on slate), Ember (warm grey, with the ember kept to what is pressed and followed) and Mono (black, white and blue). Each has a light and a dark face. The frontmatter tokens are Iris light unless a key says otherwise; the other themes swap the same roles. It is dense in the way an Operate surface should be (32px controls, 36px rows, 14px body) without being cramped.

It refuses the looks it replaced: hard-offset brutalist shadows and thick ink outlines, frosted glass, neumorphism and rainbow KPI tiles. The seven older themes (Poster, Riso, Memphis, Blueprint and Hazard as the brutal papers; Glass; Neu) remain selectable legacy families in src/styles/families/ and the frozen base sheets, but they are not this system and new work does not draw from them.
keyCharacteristics: One accent per theme; status hues are family-level and never borrowed as an accent.
Status as a tinted pill with a solid dot; spines, chart series, swimlane bars and swatches in the strong hue.
Mona Sans for the interface, JetBrains Mono for machine values.
A lifted shadow only on what floats; resting surfaces carry at most a 1px contact shadow.

rules.name: The Status Owns The Warm Side Rule
rules.body: Status hues are family-level, identical in all four themes, and no theme's accent may read as one. Ember proves it: because Failed, Suspended and Running already hold red, orange and amber, Ember's highlights are warm greys and its copper stays on what is pressed and followed.

rules.name: The One Primary Rule
rules.body: `--primary` is the theme's swatch and has the same value in light and dark for every studio theme (an e2e theme matrix asserts it). What a primary button is filled with is `--solid`, which equals the accent except in Mono.

rules.name: The Hue Is For Marks, The Tint Is For Words Rule
rules.body: A status shown as text sits in a tinted pill with deep text; a status shown as a mark (spine, bar, series, swatch, dot in the strip) uses the strong hue.

rules.name: The Machine Voice Rule
rules.body: Mono only for what a machine wrote: ids, times, durations, counts in cells, payloads. Prose about the data (side notes, placeholders, the hub name, the find field, the onset label) stays in Mona Sans.

rules.name: The No Shouting Rule
rules.body: No uppercase tracked labels and no overline kickers; hierarchy comes from weight and size alone.

rules.name: The Only What Floats Rule
rules.body: A lifted shadow means "this is above the page". Nothing at rest gets more than the contact shadow, and no shadow is ever offset.

dos: **Do** keep one accent per theme and spend it on the primary action, checked state, focus, links and the active indicator.
**Do** show status as a tinted pill with a dot in text, and as the strong hue on spines, bars, series and swatches.
**Do** draw every outline at 1px, with hairline for structure, line soft for dividers and line strong for hover and emphasis.
**Do** use 8px corners on controls and 12px on panels, fully round on pills.
**Do** keep `--primary` identical in light and dark for each theme.
**Do** give the lifted shadow only to popovers, menus, dialogs, toasts, the bulk bar, the peek and the sheet.
**Do** honour `prefers-contrast: more` (stronger lines) and `prefers-reduced-motion`; keep pill text at 4.5:1 and the ring at 3:1.
donts: **Don't** let a theme's accent, highlight, selection or active indicator be read as a status: no red, orange or amber wash, tab line or row tint (which is why Ember's highlights are warm greys), and no accent on a dot, spine or bar.
**Don't** use hard offset shadows, thick ink outlines, frosted glass, neumorphic insets or rainbow KPI tiles; those belong to the legacy families.
**Don't** add uppercase tracked kickers or eyebrow labels above headings.
**Don't** set prose, notes or placeholders in the mono face.
**Don't** animate theme or mode changes, or lift buttons on hover.
